cluster_summary: This cluster covers XSS vulnerabilities where user-supplied URLs are inserted into HTML attributes (href, src) or navigation sinks without proper validation of the URI scheme to block dangerous protocols like javascript:. It also includes cases where URLs are embedded into HTML strings without escaping (causing HTML injection) and where double quotes in URLs are not escaped (causing attribute injection). The root cause is the assumption that user-provided URLs are safe to use directly in HTML or navigation contexts.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations into redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets. Report code paths where the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 8 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization.

mechanism.missing_guard: the redirect target is accepted without constraining the final scheme and destination to trusted browser-safe values
mechanism.name: open redirect through unsafe URI scheme validation
mechanism.sink_shape: redirect responses, Location headers, OAuth/OIDC/SAML redirect validation, or browser-followed navigation targets
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, OAuth redirect_uri values, or browser navigation destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: validate redirect targets with an explicit safe-scheme and destination allowlist after decoding and normalization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Validate the URL scheme against an allowlist (e.g., http, https) or use a sanitization function that rejects script-capable protocols; only allow safe schemes; otherwise drop the attribute or use a placeholder.
sub_patterns.name: Missing URI scheme allowlist in href/src and navigation sinks
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumes user-supplied URL strings are safe HTTP/HTTPS links without validating the URI scheme, allowing dangerous schemes like javascript: to be used in href, src, window.location, or window.open.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use DOM API methods (e.g., createElement, setAttribute) to construct elements safely, ensuring automatic encoding, or apply proper HTML entity encoding before insertion.
sub_patterns.name: Missing HTML escaping in URL interpolation into HTML string
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-supplied URL is concatenated directly into an HTML string (e.g., srcdoc attribute) without HTML-escaping special characters, allowing injection of arbitrary HTML tags and scripts.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Encode double quotes as " HTML entities and properly HTML-encode the entire attribute value using a trusted encoding function.
sub_patterns.name: Missing double-quote escaping in href attribute interpolation
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled URL is inserted into an HTML attribute value (href) without escaping double quote characters, allowing attackers to break out of the attribute and inject arbitrary HTML attributes or scripts.
